definitions.explanation: A large container in a bathroom that holds water for bathing.

examples.japanese: {浴槽|よくそう}にお{湯|ゆ}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Fill the bathtub with hot water.

examples.japanese: {浴槽|よくそう}に{入|はい}ってリラックスする。
examples.english: Get into the bathtub and relax.

examples.japanese: {浴槽|よくそう}を{洗|あら}ってから{入|はい}る。
examples.english: Clean the bathtub before getting in.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{浴槽|よくそう}は{深|ふか}くて、{肩|かた}まで{浸|つ}かることができる。
examples.english: Japanese bathtubs are deep, so you can soak up to your shoulders.

examples.japanese: {浴槽|よくそう}のお{湯|ゆ}がぬるくなったので、{追|お}い{焚|だ}きして{温|あたた}め{直|なお}しました。
examples.english: The bath water cooled down, so I reheated it using the reheat function.
examples.notes: {追|お}い{焚|だ}き is the function to reheat bath water

notes:
In Japanese bathing culture, the {浴槽|よくそう} is for soaking after washing the body outside the tub ({体|からだ}を{洗|あら}ってから{入|はい}る). Family members often share the same bath water.

Types:
- FRP{製|せい} (fiberglass-reinforced plastic) - most common
- {人工|じんこう}{大理石|だいりせき} (artificial marble)
- ホーロー (enamel)
- {檜|ひのき}/{木製|もくせい} (cypress/wooden) - traditional, luxury
- ユニットバス (unit bath) - prefabricated bathroom

Colloquial terms:
- お{風呂|ふろ} (bath - general)
- バスタブ (bathtub - loanword)
- {湯船|ゆぶね} (bathtub - traditional term)

Related actions:
- お{湯|ゆ}を{張|は}る (fill the bath)
- {追|お}い{焚|だ}きする (reheat the bath water)
